settings.learner.explanationStyleScopeNo: Changing this only affects cards generated from now on. Saved words and notes are never rewritten.
The same word in the same sentence, one card from each style:
She answered with a brittle laugh and changed the subject.
The sample is written in English; the language real explanations use comes from Explanation language above.
Held together by force. Here brittle describes the laugh: it holds on the surface, but it is stretched tight and would break at a touch.
The evidence is the second half — and changed the subject. She laughs and moves the conversation on at once, so the laugh was cover, not amusement.
How to spot it: look at what it modifies. Before laugh, smile or voice it is always the figurative sense; only before glass, bone, plastic or hair does it mean literally "snaps instead of bending".
What it travels with: laugh, smile, voice, cheerfulness, politeness — all emotions held up for show.

The usual mix-up is with fragile, and the two are opposites. Fragile is weak in itself and needs careful handling; brittle is held rigid, looks fine, then gives way without warning. Of a person, fragile means "cannot take it", brittle means "barely holding and still holding".

The metaphor works through a match between a physical property and a state of mind: a brittle thing looks solid but cannot take force; move that across to a person and you get composure kept up under strain. Carrying a property from one domain to another this way is called a metaphorical mapping.
On register, the figurative brittle leans literary and turns up mostly in fiction and character description; in everyday speech a strained laugh is more often a forced laugh.
Example: His brittle cheerfulness lasted until the door closed.
A laugh forced out. It holds on the surface, but it is stretched tight and would break at a touch.
The evidence is and changed the subject — she moves the talk on straight away, so the laugh was held up on purpose.
How to spot it: followed by laugh, smile or voice it is figurative; with glass or bone it is the literal "snaps".
Goes with laugh, smile, voice, cheerfulness — all surface emotions.
Don't mix it with fragile. Fragile is weak to begin with and needs protecting; brittle is held rigid, then breaks all at once.
Example: His brittle cheerfulness lasted until the door closed.

settings.ai.servicesHint: Models are tried from top to bottom; within a model, enabled keys are tried in order before Lantern moves on. Drag the more expensive models to the end and they stay unused while one above them works.

settings.ai.vectorRetrievalHint: Also finds passages by meaning, not only the ones that share your exact words.
settings.ai.vectorRetrievalDetail: Off, Lantern finds passages that share your exact words. On, it runs both searches and merges the results, so a passage still counts when the book phrases the idea differently from your question. It uses the search model set above.
settings.ai.vectorRetrievalUnavailable: Set up and test a search model first.
settings.ai.contextLinesHint: While a book is being indexed, your chat model adds one sentence of context to each passage. That way "how did Elizabeth react when Darcy proposed" still finds the passage that only says "she was silent."
settings.ai.contextLinesDetail:
Runs once when the book is indexed, then never again. Uses the chat model from "AI services" — not the search model above — whichever your priority order puts first.

The line is only ever used for search. What the AI quotes is always the book's own wording, so a wrong line affects how well things are found, never what gets quoted.

settings.ai.embeddingDetail: This is separate from your chat models. It needs an OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint — a service that turns text into lists of numbers, so two passages can be compared by meaning instead of by wording. Lantern indexes each book once, then searches that index.

indexManager.overwriteConfirm: This will overwrite your manually edited overview and section summaries and make model calls. Continue?
indexManager.verdict.none: This book has no index yet. Once it does, the AI can cite passages from it and you can search it by meaning.
indexManager.verdict.partialBody: Right now this book only answers keyword searches. Fill them in and you can search by meaning — ask an English book a question in Chinese, or ask about "after Darcy's proposal was refused" when the book never uses those words.

indexManager.verdict.readyNoDate: The index is complete: both keyword and meaning search work.

indexManager.verdict.failed: The last index run failed. Press Finish the index to retry — whatever was already computed is kept.
indexManager.verdict.unsupported: This book's format can't be indexed yet. The AI can only read the page you're on, and search stays keyword-only.
indexManager.stopAffectsLibraryRun: This book is part of the library indexing run in progress. Stopping here stops the whole run, not just this book.

indexManager.rechunk.desc: Splits the whole book again from scratch. The vectors and summaries go stale and have to be filled in again. Only worth it when you've replaced the book's file.
indexManager.rechunk.confirmBody: The whole book gets split again. The existing {{chunks}} identity sentences, {{vectors}} vectors, section summaries and person aliases all become void and have to be generated once more.
indexManager.rechunk.confirmNote: Identity sentences, summaries and aliases are rewritten by the chat model; vectors are recomputed by the search model. Summaries you edited by hand, and aliases you taught yourself, are preserved.
indexManager.rewriteSummaries.title: Rewrite section summaries
indexManager.rewriteSummaries.desc: Rewrites only the summaries below. Chunks and vectors are left alone.
indexManager.overwriteEditedDesc: Rewrites the ones you edited by hand as well. Rewrite summaries above skips them.
indexManager.progress.background: You can close this window and keep reading — the index carries on in the background.
indexManager.progress.failed: Indexing failed during "{{phase}}". Whatever was already computed is kept; press Finish the index to pick up where it stopped.
indexManager.progress.cancelled: Stopped during "{{phase}}". Whatever was already computed is kept; the step it stopped inside runs again next time. Press Finish the index to carry on.
indexManager.aliases.title: Person aliases
indexManager.aliases.introNote: Lets you ask about this book using a translated name, a shortening, or a description like "that pastor" — even if the book itself never uses those words.
indexManager.aliases.legendNote: Tinted chips are ones you taught — they take priority over the ones found automatically.
indexManager.aliases.emptyWhat: Recognizes the people in this book, then gives each one the common translations and shortenings a reader might use.
indexManager.aliases.emptyCost: Runs once while the book is indexed; every question after that just reads the table.
indexManager.aliases.buildingHint: This can take a few minutes. Closing this window won't stop it.
indexManager.aliases.buildError.unusable: Couldn't make out who's in this book
Three tries, and each time the names that came back don't match how the book spells them — so nothing was written. Every try asks fresh, so running the same model again often works.
indexManager.aliases.buildError.invalidB: This step needs the model to answer in a fixed format, and three tries running it didn't — so nothing was written. Worth trying again; if it keeps happening, pick a different model.
indexManager.aliases.buildError.alreadyR: The earlier run hasn't finished yet. Let it finish — there's no need to start another.

bookDifficulty.why.easier: {{easy}} of the running words sit in bands 1 and 2, which you read without stopping. Only {{hard}} sit in band 4 or beyond.
bookDifficulty.why.similar: Bands 4 and 5 together hold {{hard}} of the running words, close to the {{baseline}} across the {{count}} books you have finished and analyzed.
bookDifficulty.why.harder: {{hard}} of the running words sit in bands 4 and 5; across the {{count}} books you have finished and analyzed, those two bands come to about {{baseline}}.
bookDifficulty.why.unclear: Bands 4 and 5 together hold {{hard}} of the running words. Fewer than {{min}} of your finished books have been analyzed, so there is no baseline to compare against and nothing is concluded here. The distribution below is accurate — read it yourself.
bookDifficulty.why.tooShort: {{tokens}} running words in all. Below {{floor}}, a handful of words can swing any band's share, and the comparison against your record cannot give a reliable answer. The distribution below is still a real count. It is readable; it just is not a verdict.
bookDifficulty.why.unsupported: The running text cannot be extracted from this format, so there is no distribution to count. This is not a damaged file and not a failure worth retrying — the same book in another format counts fine.
bookDifficulty.bandUnlistedHint: mostly names, places, and invented words
bookDifficulty.source: The frequency list is the top 50,000 words of the Google Books English fiction subcorpus (2010–2019).
bookDifficulty.tooShortFooter: This file will not get any longer, so there will not be a verdict here either.
bookDifficulty.unsupportedFooter: This format cannot be counted. The same book as EPUB can be.
bookDifficulty.override.body: What you pick replaces the sentence above. The automatic reading is not deleted — it stays recorded here and you can go back to it at any point. The bar and the band table are untouched either way: they are a count, not a judgement.
bookDifficulty.override.choice.hidden: Show no difficulty for this book
bookDifficulty.override.autoUnavailable: there is no automatic reading for this book
bookDifficulty.override.autoNote: The automatic reading was 「{{verdict}}」, and it is still on record.
bookDifficulty.override.autoNoteUnavaila: There is no automatic reading for this book to compare against.
bookDifficulty.override.hiddenLine: No difficulty is shown for this book.
bookCoverage.heading: This book, measured against you
bookCoverage.description: How much of this book's running text your own known words cover, per 100 words. It counts you, not a word list.
bookCoverage.unavailable: This book's coverage could not be read
bookCoverage.unavailableBody: Only this section is missing; the rest of the page is unaffected.
bookCoverage.line: The words you know cover {{share}} of {{title}}.
bookCoverage.ladder.dense: Readable now, with the dictionary open a lot
bookCoverage.ladder.independent: You can read this one on your own
bookCoverage.why.dense: Left of the 95% line. {{unknown}} words in every 100 are ones you do not know yet — roughly one a line. That does not mean you cannot read it: Lantern's look-up and annotation are built for exactly this kind of reading. It will just be slow, and closer to study than to a straight read.
bookCoverage.why.assisted: Between 95% and 98%. {{unknown}} words in every 100 are ones you do not know yet — about one every two or three lines. Readable, but with the dictionary open the whole way.
bookCoverage.why.independent: Past the 98% line. {{unknown}} words in every 100 are ones you do not know yet — one or two a page, and context will usually carry you past them. A good one to read with the dictionary shut.
bookCoverage.why.sources: This number uses nothing but your own records: {{forms}} word forms judged known to you, from the {{books}} books you have read. Names of people and places ({{nameWords}} of them, {{nameTokens}} occurrences) count as known — a name that keeps coming back costs you nothing after the first time.
bookCoverage.profileMovedOn: Your vocabulary profile has changed since these numbers were computed. To bring them up to date, use "Recompute" below.
bookCoverage.scale.floorNote: The scale starts at 88% so both lines have room to stand
bookCoverage.scale.waiting: This ruler is waiting for a reading
bookCoverage.scale.spanNote: The range crosses {{line}}, so no verdict is given here
bookCoverage.scale.pointAria: Coverage {{share}}, against the 95% and 98% reference lines
bookCoverage.scale.emptyAria: Coverage scale, with no reading on it yet
bookCoverage.compo.head: What this book's running words are made of
bookCoverage.row.mastered.name: Effortless
bookCoverage.row.mastered.hint: Passed review, or read many times without a look-up
bookCoverage.row.familiar.name: Familiar
bookCoverage.row.familiar.hint: Read a few times without a look-up, not yet effortless
bookCoverage.row.name.name: Names and places
bookCoverage.row.name.hint: Costs nothing after the first time
bookCoverage.row.unknown.name: Not known yet
bookCoverage.row.unknown.hint: Looked up and not retained, or never met
bookCoverage.footnote.familiarOn: Coverage counts "familiar" as known — counting only "effortless" gives {{alternate}}.
bookCoverage.footnote.familiarOff: Coverage counts only "effortless" — counting "familiar" too gives {{alternate}}.
bookCoverage.footnote.ruler: The two reference lines are the reading-comprehension thresholds commonly used in applied linguistics (Nation, 2006). They are a ruler, not a score.
bookCoverage.footnote.local: Everything here is computed on this machine, offline.
bookCoverage.empty.heading: Nothing is known yet about the words you know
bookCoverage.empty.body: This number is computed from your own reading records, and there is not one of them yet. Open any book and start reading — which words you met, which you looked up and which you did not, all recorded on this machine. Once there is enough, a number appears here. Until then, no guessed percentage goes in its place.
bookCoverage.empty.footnote: This section is computed entirely on this machine — no network, nothing uploaded. The book's own word-frequency distribution (the section below) needs no waiting: it has nothing to do with you and was computed at import.
bookCoverage.pending.heading: This book has not been measured yet
bookCoverage.pending.body: It means reading the whole book's word list and intersecting it with your vocabulary profile, which takes tens of seconds on a long book. Opening this page starts nothing; the button below does.
bookCoverage.running.heading: Matching the whole book against your vocabulary profile
bookCoverage.running.body: {{total}} running words in the book, {{scanned}} of them done. Leaving this page will not interrupt it, and the result stays here.
bookCoverage.running.bodyUnknown: Reading the book's word list. Leaving this page will not interrupt it, and the result stays here.
bookCoverage.stale.profileLine: This came from the vocabulary profile as it stood on {{date}}; it is being recomputed against the current one.
bookCoverage.stale.profileLineUndated: This came from the previous vocabulary profile; it is being recomputed against the current one.
bookCoverage.failed.heading: This book was not finished
bookCoverage.failed.body: The scan stopped partway. The previous result, if there was one, is still here, and you can try again.
bookCoverage.tooShort.heading: Too short to measure coverage
bookCoverage.tooShort.body: There are too few words in the text for a percentage to mean anything — a handful of words would swing it. Not shown for this book.
bookCoverage.unsupported.heading: No text could be read from this book
bookCoverage.unsupported.body: A scan, images only, or a locked-down layout — nothing countable comes out. Not shown for this book.
bookCoverage.interval.heading: Only a range can be given right now
bookCoverage.interval.body: {{forms}} word forms have been established as reliably known to you, from the {{books}} books you have read.
bookCoverage.interval.bodyFromOne: {{forms}} word forms have been established as reliably known to you, from the {{percent}}% of {{source}} you have read.
bookCoverage.interval.range: On that basis, your coverage of {{title}} is somewhere between {{low}} and {{high}}.
bookCoverage.interval.spans: That range crosses the {{line}} line, so "{{lower}}" versus "{{upper}}" cannot be told apart yet.
bookCoverage.interval.settled: The range is still wide, but both ends say the same thing: {{verdict}}.
bookCoverage.interval.footnoteSample: Where the range comes from: the records so far sit almost entirely in one or two books, and on a book of a different kind the same words might behave rather differently — so this is a range rather than a point. It narrows on its own as you read more; nothing extra is required.
bookCoverage.interval.footnoteWidth: Where the range comes from: a batch of words you have met a few times and never looked up could go either way. That batch takes up enough of this book that the two readings differ by more than a percentage point — so this is a range rather than a point. As they turn into "effortless", the range closes on its own.
bookCoverage.interval.explainBody: The low end counts only the words you read effortlessly, plus names and places; the high end adds the words that are merely familiar — the same records, read two ways. The truth is somewhere between, and nobody knows where, including you. As you read more, "familiar" turns into "effortless" and the range closes itself.
bookCoverage.words.heading: Words in {{title}} you do not know yet
bookCoverage.words.description: {{forms}} word forms, {{tokens}} occurrences in all. The ones that keep recurring come first — those are what decide how the book feels.
bookCoverage.words.empty: Not one word you do not know — you know every word in this book's text.
bookCoverage.words.groupMetaShare: {{forms}} word forms · {{tokens}} occurrences in all, {{share}} of the book
bookCoverage.words.frequentNote: Learn these and this book's coverage goes from {{from}} to {{to}} — they are packed densely enough into the text to be worth a look first.
bookCoverage.words.frequentNoteOne: Learn this one and this book's coverage goes from {{from}} to {{to}} — it is packed densely enough into the text to be worth a look first.
bookCoverage.words.frequentNoteFlat: Learning these barely moves the coverage number — but they are packed densely enough into the text that you will keep running into them, so they are worth a look first.
bookCoverage.words.frequentNoteOneFlat: Learning this one barely moves the coverage number — but it is packed densely enough into the text that you will keep running into it, so it is worth a look first.
bookCoverage.words.rareNote: This group holds the bulk of the occurrences you do not know, but each word turns up only once or twice. Learning them first pays poorly — looking one up when you reach it is enough.
bookCoverage.words.footnote: Names of people and places are not in this table ({{tokens}} occurrences of them counted as known). Nothing here goes into your word list on its own — which words to keep is yours to decide.
bookCoverage.words.collect: Add the top {{words}} to my word list
bookCoverage.sources.books.label: Books read
bookCoverage.sources.books.hint: No need to finish one; reading counts
bookCoverage.sources.books.hintThin: One more book will narrow the range noticeably
bookCoverage.sources.exposures.label: Words met
bookCoverage.sources.exposures.hint: Words that sat on screen and you did not look up
bookCoverage.sources.exposures.hintThin: Reduced to {{forms}} reliably known word forms
bookCoverage.sources.lookups.label: Look-up records
bookCoverage.sources.lookups.hint: A look-up says you did not know it then, which is also a record
bookCoverage.sources.vocab.label: Word list and review
bookCoverage.sources.vocab.hint: A word passed in review counts as known outright
bookOpenCard.settingsBody: Before you open a book for the first time, this explains what its vocabulary is made of and where the hard parts are. It shows once — the same book never gets it twice.
bookOpenCard.settingsMetaOn: On — to see these figures again later, open the book's Details page.
bookOpenCard.settingsMetaOff: Off — the full difficulty picture for each book is still on its Book Details page.
bookOpenCard.undoToastMessage: Open card turned off. You can turn it back on in Settings → Reading.
bookOpenCard.verdictReady: The words you haven't seen before in this book are {{share}}.
bookOpenCard.disclosureFootnote1: The middle column is how often you read past a word in this band rather than looking it up — the same measure the reading-level page uses. The right-hand column only shows relative weight, never a number.
bookOpenCard.disclosureFootnote2: Words outside the frequency table don't count toward this number at all. Each column is rounded on its own, so the rows won't always add up to the total exactly.
bookOpenCard.chapterPeakBody: Those chapters use noticeably heavier vocabulary than the rest of the book — reading slower there is normal. The other chapters are all about the same.
bookOpenCard.chapterFlatLine: No single stretch of this book stands out as harder.
bookOpenCard.chapterFlatBody: The vocabulary weight is about the same from start to finish — it doesn't matter which chapter you start with.
bookOpenCard.chapterBackfilling: Chapter-by-chapter detail is still catching up
bookOpenCard.chapterBackfillingBody: This book was imported a while ago, when only the whole-book figure was computed. Filling in the rest is a local re-read — no network, no AI. It will appear here on its own once it's done; no need to check back.
bookOpenCard.compareReferenceLighter: The last book you finished, “{{title}}”, was lighter than this one.
bookOpenCard.compareReferenceHeavier: The last book you finished, “{{title}}”, was heavier than this one.
bookOpenCard.compareReferenceSimilar: The last book you finished, “{{title}}”, was about the same as this one.
bookOpenCard.factsHoursAtPace: at your recent {{wpm}} words/min, about {{hours}} hours
bookOpenCard.factsHoursAtBookPace: at your {{wpm}} words/min in this book, about {{hours}} hours
bookOpenCard.verdictBookOnlyLine: About {{percent}}% of this book's words are in the 1,000 most common.
bookOpenCard.verdictBookOnlyHard: Words past rank 5,000 make up about {{percent}}%. This is just how the book itself is made — it has nothing to do with who's reading it.
bookOpenCard.insufficientNote: Whether this book runs light or heavy for you isn't something this can say yet — there isn't enough in your lookup record to work it out. Just read as you would; there's no need to look words up on purpose. Once there is enough, a line about you appears here on its own.
bookOpenCard.neverComputedHeading: This book's vocabulary hasn't been measured yet
bookOpenCard.neverComputedBody: The measurement is a local, one-time read of the full text — no network, no AI, a few seconds. It usually finishes during import; this one just missed it.
bookOpenCard.computingBody: Computed locally, no network involved. Usually a few seconds — you can start reading now, and this will fill itself in once it's done.
bookOpenCard.tooShortHeading: Too short to measure a share
bookOpenCard.tooShortBody: Only {{tokens}} words, short of the {{floor}} needed to measure. Sample chapters, forewords, and previews all end up here — and since this file won't get any longer, there's no "check back later" button for it.
bookOpenCard.unsupportedHeading: This format can't be read for its text
bookOpenCard.unsupportedBody: MOBI / AZW3 files are only measurable once converted to EPUB — the word-frequency count reads the original file, and can't reach it. The book still reads normally, it just has no difficulty figure.
bookOpenCard.genericFailedBody: The book still reads normally, it just has no difficulty figure.
bookOpenCard.staleNote: These numbers are from the previous version of the file. The text has changed since then. Measuring again takes a few seconds, and stays local either way.
bookOpenCard.scannedHeading: This is a scan — the pages are images, not text.
bookOpenCard.scannedBody: You can still turn pages and read normally, but selecting words and AI won't be able to reach the content — there's no selectable text in it. Vocabulary difficulty can't be measured for the same reason.
bookOpenCard.scannedOcrHint: One text-recognition pass fixes all of that: it runs locally, and the original file is never uploaded. The first time needs a component download (about {{size}}); after that each book is recognized once and the result is kept.
bookOpenCard.recognizingHint: Runs locally, nothing is uploaded. You can start reading now — once recognition finishes, word lookup and AI turn on automatically, and vocabulary difficulty is measured along with it.
bookOpenCard.recognitionFailedBody: You can still turn pages and read; word lookup and AI remain unavailable. You can retry once — if it still fails, the scan quality itself is likely the issue.

profile.title: User Profile
profile.loadFailed: Couldn't load the profile — you can try again.
profile.subtitle: This is what the AI reads before answering you. The top part is yours to write; the cards below are summarized from your activity — if the two disagree, what you wrote wins.
profile.subtitleOff: Your profile is off. The AI does not read this page when it answers you. What you wrote and the cards below are still here — turn it back on and they take effect again.
profile.summarizeNowOffHint: Summarizing is paused while the profile is off.
profile.strip.off: Off — no new follow-ups are being counted and nothing is summarized
profile.strip.firstBatch: New follow-ups are still accumulating — the first batch of cards appears once there are enough
profile.strip.batchProgress: New follow-ups are still accumulating — it will be re-summarized once there are enough
profile.strip.decayHint: Recent activity counts more; older activity fades
profile.strip.writeNowHint: No need to wait — the section above is ready for you right now
profile.yourText.heading: What you wrote
profile.yourText.placeholder: What you're studying for, your first language, the tone you want, anything to avoid — write it however you like. Nothing here gets touched automatically.
profile.yourText.softHint: Past the suggested length. A longer profile makes it easier for answers to miss the point, especially with lighter models. You can keep writing, or let it help you trim.
profile.yourText.draftRestored: This is what you hadn't saved last time — brought back here.
profile.system.heading: Summarized for you
profile.system.empty: Cards appear once a batch of records has built up — {{remaining}} more follow-ups to go. A follow-up means a question you asked after selecting a passage; plain word lookups don't count.
profile.evidence.unavailable: This conclusion was written before records were kept, so there's nothing to open. The next rewrite will keep them.
profile.evidence.chain: Below are the records this conclusion was written from → they produced the sentence above → that sentence goes into the prompt sent to the AI.
profile.evidence.capturedAt: Snapshot taken {{when}}; what you've read since doesn't change it.
profile.evidence.followup.summary: {{count}} follow-up questions in this dimension over the last 90 days.
profile.evidence.followup.sampleNote: {{count}} of them were shown to the AI (recent ones are likelier to be picked):
profile.evidence.lookup.summary: {{count}} lookups over the last 90 days, {{repeat}}% of them words you looked up more than once.
profile.evidence.exampleSource.summary: Your {{count}} most-read books over the last 90 days, by actual reading time:
profile.evidence.replyPacing.summary: {{count}} follow-up questions over the last 90 days, read for how you ask:
profile.evidence.replyPacing.singleTurn: {{share}}% of chats ended after a single question.
profile.injection.heading: What the AI is told about you
profile.injection.subtitle: When you ask about a passage, this goes out alongside your question. It shapes how things are explained — it is never treated as something the book says.
profile.injection.emptyProfile: Nothing is being sent yet — you haven't written anything above, and no cards have been summarized.
profile.injection.switchedOff: Your profile is switched off, so nothing is being sent to the AI.
profile.injection.scaffoldingNote: The wrapper sentences are written in English because the model reads them; your own words and the card conclusions are left exactly as they are.
profile.movedTakeoverNote: Your version above has taken over this card: it's kept here for the record only, isn't sent to the AI, and the summarizer won't touch this dimension again.
profile.move.hint: That's just a plain line of text, and the cursor is parked on it — put it in your own words, or save it as-is.
profile.move.lineRemoved: The inserted line got deleted, so nothing was moved — your other edits saved as usual.
profile.move.abandoned: That move was dropped — the card is still where it was.
profile.move.alreadyPending: Save or cancel the move already in progress before starting another one.
profile.footer.autoAnalysisHint: Triggers and usage live under Settings → Auto Analysis, including a full off switch.
profile.deleteAll.title: Delete the entire profile?
profile.deleteAll.body: This clears everything you wrote, every card, and the activity trail behind them — no partial keep, and it can't be undone.
profile.compress.title: Compressed version
profile.compress.subtitle: Compressed with a lightweight model: meaning kept, filler cut, similar requirements merged. Only this text was sent. Both boxes stay editable, and nothing changes until you press "Use this version."
profile.compress.originalStillOver: Still over the hard limit — trim it in this box and the button lights up.
profile.compress.optimizedEditable: Edit this box directly, then press "Use this version" — whatever you save is what gets kept.
profile.compress.directionLabel: Not quite right? Compress again with your own direction
profile.compress.directionPlaceholder: e.g. keep the part about my old teacher's feedback, don't compress that away
profile.compress.directionHint: Your direction is appended after the base compress instruction and sent together: the base instruction guards against dropping requirements or inventing new ones, your direction steers which way it leans. It can't override the base instruction on its own.
profile.compress.reoptimizeFailed: Re-compressing didn't go through — the version you already have is untouched, so it's safe to try again.
profile.tidy.title: Tidied version
profile.tidy.subtitle: Only reordered — nothing merged, dropped, or invented: paragraphs become one line per requirement, self-description and pleasantries go. Coming back longer is normal. Both boxes stay editable, and nothing changes until you press "Use this version."
profile.tidy.originalStillOver: Still over the limit — trim it in this box and the button lights up.
profile.tidy.optimizedEditable: Edit this box directly, then press "Use this version" — whatever you save is what gets kept.
profile.tidy.directionLabel: Not quite right? Tidy again with your own direction
profile.tidy.directionPlaceholder: e.g. group by topic instead of the order I wrote them in
profile.tidy.directionHint: Your direction is sent appended to the base instruction: the base instruction guards against merging or dropping anything, your direction only decides grouping and order.
profile.tidy.reoptimizeFailed: Re-tidying didn't go through — the version you already have is untouched, so it's safe to try again.
profile.hardLimit.title: Over the length limit
profile.hardLimit.body: This is past double the suggested length ({{softLimit}} × 2 = {{hardLimit}}). At this length, answers tend to get worse, not better — especially with lighter models. Get it under {{hardLimit}} to save.
profile.hardLimit.keep: Your draft is untouched — not one character is lost. Both manual and automatic saves land here the same way; nothing gets silently cut or rewritten for you.
profile.deleteCard.title: Delete "{{slot}}"?
profile.deleteCard.body: The AI stops using this one immediately.
profile.deleteCard.comeBackA: Possibly — but only from what you do from now on. The follow-ups behind the deleted card have already been ruled on and won't be reused.
profile.deleteCard.untouchedA: Your raw activity, every other card, and what you wrote above — none of it is touched.
profile.deleteCard.suggestMove: If it's just worded wrong, "Move up to edit" usually fits better — rewrite it your way, it sticks around, and nothing gets thrown out (plus it's reversible).
profile.errors.undo: The undo didn't go through — please try again.
profile.errors.deleteCard: Couldn't delete that card — please try again.
profile.errors.summarize: Manual summarize didn't complete — please try again.
profile.errors.toggle: Couldn't switch the profile on/off — please try again.
profile.errors.deleteAll: Couldn't delete the profile — please try again.
